title: Oven Roasted Middle Eastern Chicken Flatbread
description: A flaky, pepper‑infused flatbread crowned with tender roasted chicken, caramelized onions, and a hint of bitter sumac, perfect for a crowd‑pleasing Middle Eastern feast.
instructions: In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with olive oil, black pepper, salt, and 1 tbsp lemon juice until well coated.

Spread the chicken skins side down on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes, then flip and add sliced onions on top, continuing to roast for another 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and crispy.
While chicken roasts, roll out the laminated dough into a rectangle, dust lightly with flour, and cut into 6 equal pieces.
Brush each dough piece with a thin layer of olive oil, sprinkle with minced garlic and sumac, then place on a parchment‑lined sheet.
Bake the dough for 10 minutes, flipping halfway, until puffed and golden.
Remove chicken and onions from the oven; let rest 5 minutes, then shred the meat with a fork, discarding skin and bone.
Assemble each flatbread by placing a spoonful of shredded chicken and onions in the center, topping with chopped parsley, and folding the edges over to create a pocket.
Return assembled flatbread pockets to the oven for 5 minutes to warm through.
Serve hot, accompanied by a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
